paras.en: Now, Montgomery-Haga hopes those struggles are finally coming to an end. That’s because a clinical trial with an experimental therapy has helped restore mobility for her — and others like her. She can stride through her living room again. She can landscape her front yard. She doesn’t have to brace herself when her dogs jump on her. And she hasn’t fallen once since the treatment. The change has been drastic, she says. “I’m just really excited about the future.”
paras.zh: 现在，蒙哥马利-哈加希望这些斗争最终能够结束。这是因为一项实验性疗法的临床试验帮助她和其他像她一样的人恢复了活动能力。她又可以大步穿过客厅了。她可以美化她的前院。当她的狗扑向她时，她不必支撑自己。自从接受治疗以来，她再也没有跌倒过一次。她说，变化是巨大的。 “我对未来感到非常兴奋。”

paras.en: The treatment, a type of CAR T cell therapy, extracts immune cells from a person’s body and engineers them to attack the very cells causing the disease. First used to fight cancer, CAR T is now also targeting a variety of autoimmune diseases. If given the green light by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, Montgomery-Haga’s treatment would be the first such therapy approved for an autoimmune condition — and it would be the first approved treatment for stiff person syndrome.
paras.zh: 这种疗法是一种 CAR T 细胞疗法，从人体内提取免疫细胞，并改造它们来攻击引起疾病的细胞。 CAR T 最初用于对抗癌症，现在也用于治疗多种自身免疫性疾病。如果获得美国食品和药物管理局的批准，蒙哥马利-哈加的治疗将是第一个被批准用于自身免疫性疾病的治疗方法，并且这将是第一个被批准用于僵人综合症的治疗方法。

paras.en: Stiff person syndrome may be just the beginning, says Carl June, the University of Pennsylvania immunologist and oncologist who spearheaded CAR T cell therapy for cancer decades ago. The “living drug” could herald a new era of therapeutics for autoimmune diseases like lupus, rheumatoid arthritis and even multiple sclerosis. “It’s revolutionary to think how far things have gone,” June says.
paras.zh: 宾夕法尼亚大学免疫学家和肿瘤学家卡尔·琼 (Carl June) 表示，僵人综合症可能只是一个开始，几十年前他率先提出了 CAR T 细胞治疗癌症的方法。这种“活体药物”可能预示着狼疮、类风湿性关节炎甚至多发性硬化症等自身免疫性疾病治疗的新时代。 “想想事情已经走了多远，这是革命性的，”琼说。

paras.en: But he warns that it’s far too early to know if scientists have definitively cured stiff person syndrome. And there haven’t been enough people treated to get a good handle on all the possible side effects. “There could be long-term complications in autoimmune patients that don’t happen in our cancer patients,” he says. Other researchers urge caution. “It’s very important not to oversell it,” says Marc Scherlinger, a rheumatologist at Strasbourg University Hospital in France.
paras.zh: 但他警告说，现在判断科学家是否已经彻底治愈僵人综合症还为时过早。而且还没有足够多的人接受治疗来很好地处理所有可能的副作用。 “自身免疫患者可能会出现长期并发症，而我们的癌症患者不会发生这种情况，”他说。其他研究人员敦促谨慎行事。 “不要过度吹捧它，这一点非常重要，”法国斯特拉斯堡大学医院的风湿病学家马克·谢林格 (Marc Scherlinger) 说。

paras.en: For Piquet, one crucial question is how long the treatment will last. In Montgomery-Haga’s case, the answer seems to be at least two years. Montgomery-Haga still considers herself disabled, or “disabled-ish,” as she calls it. But when rating how she used to feel on a scale of one to 10, she’d put herself at a zero before treatment, she says. These days, she’s more like a seven.
paras.zh: 对于皮奎特来说，一个关键问题是治疗能持续多久。在蒙哥马利-哈加的例子中，答案似乎是至少两年。蒙哥马利-哈加仍然认为自己是残疾人，或者用她的话说，“有点残疾人”。但她说，当用 1 到 10 的等级来评估她过去的感受时，她在治疗前将自己的评分为零。如今，她更像是一个七岁的人了。

paras.en: What’s more, Montgomery-Haga says, “I think I’m still improving.”
paras.zh: 更重要的是，蒙哥马利-哈加说，“我认为我仍在进步。”

paras.en: There’s no single symptom that clued Montgomery-Haga in to her disease. In 2014, she started having difficulty picking things up off the floor. Then her boss asked her why she was limping — Montgomery-Haga hadn’t noticed. Her balance was off and her head felt weird, like “I was walking around in a fishbowl,” she says. It got to the point where Montgomery-Haga had difficulty crossing thresholds between rooms.
paras.zh: 没有任何单一症状表明蒙哥马利-哈加患有她的疾病。 2014年，她开始难以拾起地板上的东西。然后她的老板问她为什么一瘸一拐——蒙哥马利-哈加没有注意到。她失去了平衡，头感觉很奇怪，就像“我在鱼缸里走来走去”，她说。蒙哥马利-哈加已经很难跨过房间之间的门槛了。

paras.en: Montgomery-Haga would startle easily, prompting her body to stiffen up like a board. One time when cooking, she burned her finger, spasmed and collapsed, cracking the back of her head on the cabinets. She lay on the floor crying, but finally managed to right herself. “As soon as you hit the floor,” she says, “your muscles are like, ‘Fine,’ and you can get up again.”
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加很容易受惊，身体就会像木板一样僵硬。有一次做饭时，她的手指被烫伤，痉挛并倒下，后脑勺撞到了柜子上。她躺在地板上哭泣，但最终还是站了起来。 “一旦你落地，”她说，“你的肌肉就会说，‘很好’，你就可以再次站起来了。”

paras.en: Those unpredictable symptoms capture a slice of what life is like with stiff person syndrome, or SPS. The disease, which affects roughly 2 in 100,000 people in the United States, typically develops in a person’s 30s or 40s. It is about twice as common in women as in men.
paras.zh: 这些不可预测的症状反映了僵人综合症（SPS）的生活情况。在美国，这种疾病大约影响十万分之二的人，通常在 30 多岁或 40 多岁时发病。女性的发病率约为男性的两倍。

paras.en: Scientists don’t know what sets off the disease. But they think a person’s own antibodies start attacking a neurological network that helps muscles throughout the body relax. And when those tensed muscles are in opposition, like the biceps and triceps, they start fighting one another, Piquet says. That’s when people can end up in a stuck position, leading to stiffness. But because everyone’s immune system is different, patients’ experiences with the disease can vary greatly.
paras.zh: 科学家们不知道是什么引发了这种疾病。但他们认为，一个人自身的抗体开始攻击帮助全身肌肉放松的神经网络。皮奎特说，当那些紧张的肌肉（例如二头肌和三头肌）处于对立状态时，它们就会开始互相对抗。这时人们可能会陷入困境，导致僵硬。但由于每个人的免疫系统不同，患者的疾病经历可能会有很大差异。

paras.en: For Tara Zier, a former dentist based in Maryland, SPS started with extreme neck pain, blood pressure spikes, shortness of breath and feelings of impending doom. While some people struggle with mobility, Zier’s difficulties include standing and extreme fatigue. When she holds herself upright, her muscles clamp down on her spine like it’s in a vise. “Have you ever had a charley horse in your calf?” she asks. “Imagine one in your whole body that stops you in your tracks.”
paras.zh: 塔拉·齐尔 (Tara Zier) 是马里兰州的一名前牙医，SPS 开始时伴随着颈部极度疼痛、血压飙升、呼吸急促和厄运即将来临的感觉。虽然有些人行动不便，但齐尔的困难包括站立和极度疲劳。当她直立时，她的肌肉会像虎钳一样夹紧脊柱。 “你的小腿里曾经养过查理马吗？”她问。 “想象一下你全身有一个东西让你停下来。”

paras.en: Zier and Montgomery-Haga went years before learning what was behind their symptoms. Their cases mystified doctors — Zier saw 13 specialists and visited the emergency room nine times before getting a diagnosis. When she finally found out she had SPS three years after her first symptoms, Zier says she felt validated, like medicine was confirming what she already knew: “Something’s wrong with me.”
paras.zh: 齐尔和蒙哥马利-哈加花了很多年才了解他们症状背后的原因。他们的病例让医生感到困惑——齐尔在得到诊断之前看了 13 名专家并去了急诊室 9 次。齐尔说，当她在首次出现症状三年后终于发现自己患有 SPS 时，她感到自己得到了认可，就像医学证实了她已经知道的事情一样：“我有些问题。”

paras.en: Montgomery-Haga’s 2018 diagnosis put her “over the moon,” she says. For nearly four years, she had gotten sicker and sicker — but doctors couldn’t tell her why. She felt as if they were giving up on her. With the diagnosis, Montgomery-Haga not only learned that SPS existed, she says, “I was told it’s treatable.”
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加 2018 年的诊断让她“欣喜若狂”，她说。近四年来，她的病情越来越严重，但医生却无法告诉她原因。她觉得他们好像要放弃她了。通过诊断，蒙哥马利-哈加不仅了解到 SPS 的存在，她说，“我还被告知这是可以治疗的。”

paras.en: Current treatments include muscle relaxers, anti-seizure medications and Botox injections in body parts that feel especially stiff. Although these off-label therapies can address people’s symptoms, they’re “doing nothing to treat the underlying autoimmune disease,” Piquet says. And some can come with potent side effects, like mental fog.
paras.zh: 目前的治疗方法包括肌肉松弛剂、抗癫痫药物以及在感觉特别僵硬的身体部位注射肉毒杆菌。皮奎特说，尽管这些标签外疗法可以解决人们的症状，但它们“对治疗潜在的自身免疫性疾病没有任何作用”。有些可能会带来强烈的副作用，比如精神迷雾。

paras.en: Zier, who has tried multiple combinations of different meds, remembers frequently losing her train of thought. She has since tapered off all but one drug, a low dose of Valium. “The trade-off,” she says, “is pain.”
paras.zh: 齐尔尝试过不同药物的多种组合，她记得经常失去思路。此后，她逐渐减少了除一种药物（低剂量的安定）外的所有药物的用量。 “代价是，”她说，“就是痛苦。”

paras.en: People with SPS can also receive intravenous infusions of healthy antibodies, a treatment called IVIG, to decrease muscle spasms and stiffness. Montgomery-Haga found it helpful but time-consuming. She’d go to the clinic every three weeks for an infusion, which could take up to six hours.
paras.zh: 患有 SPS 的人还可以接受静脉注射健康抗体（一种称为 IVIG 的治疗方法），以减少肌肉痉挛和僵硬。蒙哥马利-哈加发现这很有帮助，但很耗时。她每三周去一次诊所输液，这可能需要长达六个小时。

paras.en: “The bottom line is there are no FDA-approved therapies for this disease,” Piquet says. Now, the one most likely to cross the finish line first is something no one would have expected even a few years ago, CAR T pioneer June says. If you told doctors that CAR T cell therapy was going to be FDA approved for an autoimmune disease, he says, “people would have laughed.”
paras.zh: “最重要的是，目前还没有 FDA 批准的治疗这种疾病的疗法，”皮奎特说。 CAR T 先驱 June 表示，现在，最有可能第一个冲过终点线的人即使在几年前也没有人预料到。他说，如果你告诉医生 CAR T 细胞疗法将获得 FDA 批准用于治疗自身免疫性疾病，“人们会笑的。”

paras.en: June may be best known for his work in cancer, but he’s been keenly following the progress in auto-immune therapy. His daughter, now in her 30s, was diagnosed with juvenile rheumatoid arthritis when she was 9 years old. For her, that’s meant over 20 years of treatment with drugs that bring a bundle of side effects, such as fatigue and risk of infections. “It would be much better to be cured,” he says.
paras.zh: 琼最出名的可能是他在癌症方面的工作，但他一直在密切关注自身免疫治疗的进展。他的女儿现年30多岁，9岁时被诊断出患有幼年类风湿性关节炎。对她来说，这意味着 20 多年的药物治疗会带来一系列副作用，例如疲劳和感染风险。 “如果能被治愈就更好了，”他说。

paras.en: In autoimmune diseases like rheumatoid arthritis, lupus and SPS, a person’s own antibodies attack tissues throughout the body, from blood vessels to cartilage to neurons. Wiping out these rogue antibodies can stop the attacks. But CAR T cell therapy doesn’t act on the antibodies themselves. It goes straight to the source, snuffing out the cellular factories that manufacture them.
paras.zh: 在类风湿性关节炎、狼疮和 SPS 等自身免疫性疾病中，人体自身的抗体会攻击全身的组织，从血管到软骨再到神经元。消灭这些流氓抗体可以阻止攻击。但 CAR T 细胞疗法并不作用于抗体本身。它直达源头，消灭制造它们的细胞工厂。

paras.en: Those antibody factories are known as B cells. To eliminate them, doctors recruit T cells, which act as the body’s security system and work together to hunt down and destroy problematic cells. In the lab, scientists fine-tune these hunters, outfitting them with a molecular homing device called a chimeric antigen receptor, or CAR. When infused back into patients’ bodies, the newly-engineered T cells can target the antibody factories directly — like a saboteur told exactly what to destroy.
paras.zh: 这些抗体工厂被称为 B 细胞。为了消除它们，医生招募 T 细胞，它们充当人体的安全系统，共同努力追捕并摧毁有问题的细胞。在实验室里，科学家们对这些猎人进行了微调，为它们配备了一种称为嵌合抗原受体（CAR）的分子归巢装置。当重新注入患者体内时，新设计的 T 细胞可以直接瞄准抗体工厂——就像破坏者确切地告诉要破坏什么一样。

paras.en: The CAR T cell therapy Lynn Montgomery-Haga received wipes out B cells, including the ones likely driving her disease. Doctors hope this therapy “resets” her immune system, getting rid of harmful B cells and letting healthy new ones take their place.
paras.zh: Lynn Montgomery-Haga 接受的 CAR T 细胞疗法消除了 B 细胞，包括可能导致她患病的细胞。医生希望这种疗法能够“重置”她的免疫系统，消除有害的 B 细胞，让健康的新细胞取而代之。

paras.en: “The secret behind CAR T cell therapy is that you completely deplete B cells in the body,” says Georg Schett, a rheumatologist at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg in Germany. Temporarily wiping out a person’s B cells lets the body replace them with fresh, unproblematic ones, Schett says. He calls it an “immune reset.”
paras.zh: “CAR T 细胞疗法背后的秘密是完全耗尽体内的 B 细胞，”德国埃尔兰根-纽伦堡弗里德里希-亚历山大大学的风湿病学家 Georg Schett 说。谢特说，暂时清除一个人的 B 细胞可以让身体用新鲜的、没有问题的 B 细胞取而代之。他称之为“免疫重置”。

paras.en: CAR T cell therapy got its start in the 2010s, when researchers used engineered T cells to target cancer. In 2017, the FDA approved the first CAR T cell therapies for two blood cancers, acute lymphoblastic leukemia and large B cell lymphoma. Soon after, scientists saw the first tantalizing hints that it might work for autoimmune diseases, too. In some cases, cancer patients with autoimmune disorders reported improvements in both conditions after treatment.
paras.zh: CAR T 细胞疗法始于 2010 年代，当时研究人员使用工程 T 细胞来靶向癌症。 2017年，FDA批准了首个CAR T细胞疗法用于治疗两种血癌：急性淋巴细胞白血病和大B细胞淋巴瘤。不久之后，科学家们看到了第一个诱人的迹象，表明它也可能对自身免疫性疾病有效。在某些情况下，患有自身免疫性疾病的癌症患者报告说，治疗后这两种情况都有所改善。

paras.en: But most researchers didn’t think it could be that easy, Schett says. After all, autoimmune diseases were driven by a complex network of cell types. How could targeting just one of them work?
paras.zh: 但大多数研究人员认为事情没那么容易，谢特说。毕竟，自身免疫性疾病是由复杂的细胞类型网络驱动的。只针对其中一个怎么可能有效呢？

paras.en: That thinking underwent a paradigm shift in 2021 when Schett and his team published the first major paper reporting a successful treatment with the therapy. The patient was a 20-year-old woman with a severe case of lupus, a complex, sometimes-fatal illness that can damage the kidneys and other organs. Within five weeks of CAR T cell therapy treatment, signs of her disease began to vanish.
paras.zh: 2021 年，当 Schett 和他的团队发表了第一篇报告该疗法成功治疗的重要论文时，这种想法发生了范式转变。患者是一名 20 岁女性，患有严重的狼疮，这是一种复杂的、有时甚至致命的疾病，会损害肾脏和其他器官。在接受 CAR T 细胞疗法治疗五周内，她的疾病迹象开始消失。

paras.en: Results like these were “unheard of,” says rheumatologist Maximilian Konig of Johns Hopkins Medicine in Baltimore. Lupus is extremely difficult to treat, and for decades, most drugs tested against it failed. No one had ever seen the kind of improvements that Schett’s patient experienced.
paras.zh: 巴尔的摩约翰·霍普金斯医学院的风湿病学家马克西米利安·科尼格说，这样的结果“闻所未闻”。狼疮极难治疗，几十年来，大多数针对狼疮的药物测试都失败了。没有人见过谢特的病人所经历的那种改善。

paras.en: After the paper came out, “everybody was talking about it,” Konig says. Today, more than five years later, the woman’s lupus hasn’t returned, Schett says. “We consider this patient cured,” he says.
paras.zh: 论文发表后，“每个人都在谈论它，”科尼格说。谢特说，五年多后的今天，这位女士的狼疮还没有复发。 “我们认为这名患者已经治愈，”他说。

paras.en: The woman’s response was no fluke. The following year, Schett’s team reported similar results in five more lupus patients. All went into remission after CAR T cell therapy.
paras.zh: 女人的反应并非侥幸。第二年，谢特的团队在另外五名狼疮患者中报告了类似的结果。 CAR T 细胞治疗后，所有患者的病情均得到缓解。

paras.en: This was the true tipping point, June says. “It’s rare, very rare, that you get such striking results.”
paras.zh: 琼说，这是真正的转折点。 “能得到如此惊人的结果，非常罕见。”

paras.en: What followed was an explosion of research around the world. Scientists are now testing CAR T cell therapy in nearly a dozen autoimmune diseases linked to harmful B cells, including lupus, rheumatoid arthritis and a connective-tissue disease known as systemic sclerosis.
paras.zh: 随之而来的是世界各地研究的爆炸式增长。科学家们目前正在测试 CAR T 细胞疗法治疗近十几种与有害 B 细胞相关的自身免疫性疾病，包括狼疮、类风湿性关节炎和一种称为系统性硬化症的结缔组织疾病。

paras.en: Kyverna, the California-based company behind the SPS trial, is also running trials for neurological autoimmune conditions including generalized myasthenia gravis and progressive multiple sclerosis, or MS.
paras.zh: Kyverna 是一家总部位于加利福尼亚州的 SPS 试验背后的公司，该公司还在针对神经系统自身免疫性疾病进行试验，包括全身性重症肌无力和进行性多发性硬化症 (MS)。

paras.en: One reason using CAR T cell therapy for neurological conditions excites researchers is because of the cells’ potential to slip past the blood-brain barrier. That means they might be able to access pockets of smoldering inflammation inaccessible to other drugs, says neurologist Rebecca Farber of Columbia University.
paras.zh: 使用 CAR T 细胞疗法治疗神经系统疾病让研究人员兴奋的原因之一是这些细胞具有穿过血脑屏障的潜力。哥伦比亚大学神经学家丽贝卡·法伯说，这意味着它们可能能够接触到其他药物无法接触到的闷烧炎症区域。

paras.en: That could be a huge help in diseases like MS, in which a person’s antibodies attack the protective sheaths around nerve cells, causing numbness, brain fog and difficulty walking. Still, Farber doubts that CAR T cell therapy could fix existing damage. “We’re not expecting it to repair the nervous system,” she says. But it’s possible the treatment could freeze the disease’s progress. Patients are already asking her team about future treatments.
paras.zh: 这可能对治疗多发性硬化症等疾病有很大帮助，在这种疾病中，人的抗体会攻击神经细胞周围的保护鞘，导致麻木、脑雾和行走困难。尽管如此，法伯仍怀疑 CAR T 细胞疗法能否修复现有损伤。 “我们并不指望它能修复神经系统，”她说。但这种治疗有可能阻止疾病的进展。患者已经向她的团队询问未来的治疗方法。

paras.en: For Piquet, who cares for roughly 100 people with SPS, Kyverna’s trial offered a compelling opportunity to help her patients. Montgomery-Haga cried when Piquet told her about the trial at one of their regular Zoom appointments. She recalls wondering, is this the treatment that “might help me be normal again?”
paras.zh: 对于负责照顾大约 100 名 SPS 患者的 Piquet 来说，Kyverna 的试验为帮助她的患者提供了一个令人信服的机会。当皮奎特在他们定期的 Zoom 约会中告诉蒙哥马利-哈加有关审判时，蒙哥马利-哈加哭了。她回忆道，她当时想，这种治疗“可能会帮助我恢复正常吗？”

paras.en: The good, the bad and the potentially ugly
paras.zh: 好的、坏的和潜在的丑陋

paras.en: Though Montgomery-Haga leapt at the chance to try Kyverna’s treatment, called miv-cel, CAR T cell therapy is no walk in the park. Before starting, doctors sit patients down to “talk about the good, the bad and the potentially ugly,” Piquet says.
paras.zh: 尽管 Montgomery-Haga 抓住了机会尝试 Kyverna 的治疗方法 miv-cel，但 CAR T 细胞疗法并不是在公园里散步。皮奎特说，在开始之前，医生会让病人坐下来“谈论好的、坏的和可能丑陋的事情”。

paras.en: That includes the rigorous prep work needed before people receive their engineered T cells. Patients must first get low-dose chemotherapy, which flushes T cells from the body and makes space for the new ones. Chemo can ambush the body with symptoms including hair thinning, nausea, vomiting and diarrhea.
paras.zh: 这包括人们接受工程 T 细胞之前所需的严格准备工作。患者必须首先接受低剂量化疗，将 T 细胞从体内清除，并为新细胞腾出空间。化疗可能会给身体带来一些症状，包括头发稀疏、恶心、呕吐和腹泻。

paras.en: Treatment itself also carries risks. It destroys most B cells in the body — not just the ones that cause disease. That can lead to fever, inflammation and potentially risky infections. In Kyverna’s trial, for example, 15 percent of participants had severely low white blood cell counts after treatment. Such symptoms were expected, Piquet says, and were easily treated.
paras.zh: 治疗本身也存在风险。它会破坏体内的大多数 B 细胞，而不仅仅是导致疾病的 B 细胞。这可能会导致发烧、炎症和潜在的危险感染。例如，在 Kyverna 的试验中，15% 的参与者在治疗后白细胞计数严重偏低。皮奎特说，这种症状是预料之中的，而且很容易治疗。

paras.en: Other CAR T treatments seem to have fared far worse. In August, the pharmaceutical company Novartis paused clinical trials of its therapy, rap-cel, across a spectrum of autoimmune diseases after three patients died. Bristol Myers Squibb has also paused similar studies after some patients experienced neurological complications, according to the Wall Street Journal. Details of the incidents were slow to emerge and have set the field on edge. “It’s a tragedy,” Konig says. He calls such outcomes an important wake-up call.
paras.zh: 其他 CAR T 疗法的效果似乎要差得多。八月，诺华制药公司在三名患者死亡后暂停了其治疗多种自身免疫性疾病的疗法 rap-cel 的临床试验。据《华尔街日报》报道，在一些患者出现神经系统并发症后，百时美施贵宝也暂停了类似的研究。事件的细节慢慢浮出水面，让业界感到紧张。 “这是一场悲剧，”科尼格说。他称这些结果是一个重要的警钟。

paras.en: But red flags in one trial don’t mean all CAR T products are dangerous, Konig says. That’s because many different designs and manufacturing processes exist, and scientists can’t always predict what will make one product toxic and another safe. Kyverna’s miv-cel, for instance, has been consistently well-tolerated in the more than 100 patients treated, a spokesperson for the company says.
paras.zh: 但科尼格说，一项试验中的危险信号并不意味着所有 CAR T 产品都是危险的。这是因为存在许多不同的设计和制造工艺，科学家无法总能预测什么会使一种产品有毒而另一种产品安全。例如，该公司发言人表示，Kyverna 的 miv-cel 在 100 多名接受治疗的患者中一直表现出良好的耐受性。

paras.en: CAR T cell therapies are transformative, Konig says. “They’re going to change the field — but there are risks.”
paras.zh: Konig 说，CAR T 细胞疗法具有变革性。 “他们将改变这个领域——但也存在风险。”

paras.en: Another risk is that the once-vanquished disease will return. Doctors don’t know all the genetic and environmental conditions that trigger autoimmune disease. Some researchers wonder whether vulnerable individuals remain vulnerable, even after treatment. But because it often takes multiple insults for someone to tip into a state of disease, Scherlinger says, CAR T cell therapy could buy patients lots of time.
paras.zh: 另一个风险是曾经被战胜的疾病将会卷土重来。医生并不了解引发自身免疫性疾病的所有遗传和环境条件。一些研究人员想知道，即使在接受治疗后，脆弱的个体是否仍然脆弱。但谢林格表示，由于一个人往往需要多次受到伤害才会陷入疾病状态，因此 CAR T 细胞疗法可以为患者赢得大量时间。

paras.en: After 10 days in the hospital for her treatment, Montgomery-Haga returned to recover at home. In the following months, she started to notice some changes. It was easier getting around the house, for one. And she felt her balance and stability improving. She can now kneel down to garden and clean without the days of recovery it used to require. “I can vacuum my house,” she says. “It seems so little, but now I can vacuum!”
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加在医院接受治疗 10 天后，回到家中康复。在接下来的几个月里，她开始注意到一些变化。一方面，在房子里走动更容易。她感觉自己的平衡性和稳定性有所改善。她现在可以跪在花园里打扫卫生，而无需像以前那样需要几天的恢复时间。 “我可以给我的房子吸尘，”她说。 “看起来很小，但现在我可以吸尘了！”

paras.en: Montgomery-Haga can even sit down “crisscross applesauce,” she says. “I couldn’t do that for, like, 10 years.”
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加甚至可以坐下来“纵横交错的苹果酱”，她说。 “我大概有 10 年都做不到这一点。”

paras.en: Four months after the treatment, Piquet’s team tested Montgomery-Haga’s walking ability. In a hallway at University of Colorado Anschutz’s research building, the team marked out 25 feet with little orange cones. At one end stood Montgomery-Haga. At the other, Piquet watched behind a video camera. This time, Montgomery-Haga’s gait was smooth and her arms were down, not hovering out into the air to catch herself if she fell. “You could see that she was walking with a lot more confidence,” Piquet says.
paras.zh: 治疗四个月后，皮奎特的团队测试了蒙哥马利-哈加的步行能力。在科罗拉多大学安舒茨分校研究大楼的走廊里，研究小组用橙色小锥体标记了 25 英尺。蒙哥马利-哈加站在一端。另一方面，皮奎特在摄像机后面观看。这一次，蒙哥马利-哈加的步态平稳，双臂垂下，不会在摔倒时悬停在空中接住自己。 “你可以看到她走路时更加自信了，”皮奎特说。

paras.en: The team saw similar results in other SPS patients. Some who had difficulty walking before treatment now wanted to run, Piquet says. “It’s incredible to just see those patients speeding down the hallway.” She remembers smiles, high fives and a sense of celebration in the air. Eight of 12 people who had used a walking aid for the initial test didn’t need one for the follow-up, Piquet reported at the American Academy of Neurology meeting in April.
paras.zh: 研究小组在其他 SPS 患者中也看到了类似的结果。皮奎特说，一些在治疗前行走困难的人现在想跑步。 “看到那些病人在走廊上疾驰，真是令人难以置信。”她记得微笑、击掌和空气中的庆祝气氛。皮奎特在 4 月份的美国神经病学学会会议上报告说，在初次测试中使用助行器的 12 人中有 8 人在后续测试中不需要助行器。

paras.en: In September, Kyverna reported the trial’s one-year results: Patients maintained mobility improvements, with a third completing their 25-foot walk about as fast as a healthy adult. Additionally, nearly all patients no longer rely on immuno-suppressive drugs to tamp down harmful immune activity. That’s good news because such drugs can bring all sorts of nasty side effects, like vomiting, bleeding and infections.
paras.zh: 9 月，Kyverna 报告了该试验的一年结果：患者的活动能力保持改善，三分之一的患者完成 25 英尺步行的速度与健康成年人的速度相当。此外，几乎所有患者都不再依赖免疫抑制药物来抑制有害的免疫活动。这是个好消息，因为此类药物会带来各种令人讨厌的副作用，如呕吐、出血和感染。

paras.en: The results with SPS are “really something to celebrate,” June says. But only time and many more treatments will reveal how safe CAR T really is, he says.
paras.zh: June 说，SPS 的结果“确实值得庆祝”。但他说，只有时间和更多的治疗才能揭示 CAR T 的真正安全性。

paras.en: That’s a concern for Zier, who says she wouldn’t feel comfortable trying the therapy at this point. Zier doesn’t know how she’d respond. She’s a single mother with two kids; even a rare side effect could disrupt her life in a way she may not be able to manage. And these days, she’s managing as well as she can. Zier is the founder and CEO of The Stiff Person Syndrome Research Foundation, which supports research for SPS treatments.
paras.zh: 这是齐尔担心的问题，她说她现在不愿意尝试这种疗法。紫儿不知道自己会作何反应。她是一位有两个孩子的单亲妈妈；即使是罕见的副作用也可能以她无法应对的方式扰乱她的生活。如今，她已经尽力做到最好了。 Zier 是僵人综合症研究基金会的创始人兼首席执行官，该基金会支持 SPS 治疗研究。

paras.en: Kyverna is in the process of submitting miv-cel for FDA approval. The company is seeking priority review and hopes the treatment might be available to patients in 2027. If SPS is the first autoimmune disease to have an FDA-approved CAR T cell therapy, myasthenia gravis could be the second, says Warner Biddle, Kyverna’s CEO. What’s more, miv-cel also appeared to improve symptoms in six patients with severe cases of rheumatoid arthritis, researchers reported in August in Nature Medicine.
paras.zh: Kyverna 正在向 FDA 提交 miv-cel 的批准。该公司正在寻求优先审查，并希望在 2027 年为患者提供该治疗方法。Kyverna 首席执行官 Warner Biddle 表示，如果 SPS 是第一个获得 FDA 批准的 CAR T 细胞疗法的自身免疫性疾病，那么重症肌无力可能是第二个。此外，研究人员在 8 月的《自然医学》杂志上报道称，miv-cel 似乎还改善了 6 名严重类风湿关节炎患者的症状。

paras.en: As for what’s next, the door is wide open. Some scientists are working to make off-the-shelf forms of CAR T that wouldn’t require personalized engineering. Others are trying to reprogram T cells directly inside people’s bodies, rather than in the lab. Still others are trying to make T cells that target only the B cells responsible for disease. In the future, doctors might use such drugs to help patients avoid the cumbersome treatment process that Montgomery-Haga endured.
paras.zh: 至于接下来的事情，大门是敞开的。一些科学家正在致力于制造不需要个性化工程的现成 CAR T 形式。其他人则试图直接在人体内而不是在实验室中对 T 细胞进行重新编程。还有一些人正在尝试制造只针对导致疾病的 B 细胞的 T 细胞。未来，医生可能会使用此类药物来帮助患者避免蒙哥马利-哈加所经历的繁琐治疗过程。

paras.en: Montgomery-Haga’s own future looks far different than what she had imagined a few years ago. In 2026, she took a trip to Washington, D.C., to see the monuments. Now she’d like to visit Paris, Scotland and Ireland, too.
paras.zh: 蒙哥马利-哈加自己的未来看起来与她几年前的想象大不相同。 2026年，她前往华盛顿特区参观了这些纪念碑。现在她也想去巴黎、苏格兰和爱尔兰。

paras.en: For so many years, Montgomery-Haga has looked at trips and activities — and even household chores — that most people take for granted, thinking, “Man, I wish I could do that,” she says. “Now I can.”
paras.zh: 多年来，蒙哥马利-哈加一直关注大多数人认为理所当然的旅行和活动，甚至家务，她说：“伙计，我希望我能做到这一点。” “现在我可以了。”

articles.title: Was van Gogh’s ‘The Starry Night’ a flight of fancy or a real sky?
articles.author: Lisa Grossman

paras.en: Vincent van Gogh’s “The Starry Night” may have been based on one specific night sky: July 22, 1889, just before dawn over France.
paras.zh: 文森特·梵高的《星夜》可能是基于一个特定的夜空：1889 年 7 月 22 日，法国黎明前夕。

paras.en: If that’s true, it means the famous painting was based on real observations, not just van Gogh’s imagination, astronomer Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim and colleagues report October 22 in Scientific Reports.
paras.zh: 天文学家 Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim 及其同事 10 月 22 日在《科学报告》中报道，如果这是真的，则意味着这幅名画是基于真实的观察，而不仅仅是梵高的想象。

paras.en: “How could an invented sky fit the sky of a particular date this closely?” the team writes. “Observation and imagination have commonly been treated as an either/or, yet ‘The Starry Night’ shows the two coexisting on one canvas.”
paras.zh: “一个虚构的天空怎么可能与特定日期的天空如此贴合呢？”该团队写道。 “观察和想象通常被视为非此即彼，但《星夜》却将两者共存于一张画布上。”

paras.en: Art historians typically date “The Starry Night” to mid-June 1889, based on one of van Gogh’s letters to his brother Theo.
paras.zh: 艺术史学家通常根据梵高写给弟弟西奥的一封信，将《星夜》的创作日期定为 1889 年 6 月中旬。

paras.en: “At last I have a landscape with olive trees, and also a new study of a starry sky,” van Gogh wrote on or about June 18. About a month earlier, van Gogh had entered a hospital in Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, France. “The Starry Night” is thought to represent the view through the window of his room. A short time later, van Gogh experienced an illness during which he didn’t paint for about six weeks, so most historians think “The Starry Night” must have been painted before then.
paras.zh: 梵高在 6 月 18 日左右写道：“我终于有了一幅有橄榄树的风景画，还有对星空的新研究。”大约一个月前，梵高住进了法国圣雷米普罗旺斯的一家医院。 “星夜”被认为代表了透过他房间窗户看到的景色。不久之后，梵高得了一场病，大约六个星期没有画画，所以大多数历史学家认为《星夜》一定是在那之前画的。

paras.en: That letter is taken as strong evidence, says astronomer Donald Olson of Texas State University in San Marcos, who has written about how astronomy shows up in art history. Historians favor the June date because “van Gogh himself said so,” he says.
paras.zh: 德克萨斯州立大学圣马科斯分校的天文学家唐纳德·奥尔森曾撰写过有关天文学如何出现在艺术史中的文章，他说，这封信被视为强有力的证据。历史学家赞成六月这一日期，因为“梵高本人就是这么说的，”他说。

paras.en: That assumption has led to some confusion, though. In the 1980s, two astronomers tried to match the painting’s stars to real skies in Saint-Rémy in mid-June. One proposed that the sky was from June 19, 1889, and the collection of swirly stars is the constellation Aries.
paras.zh: 不过，这种假设导致了一些混乱。 20 世纪 80 年代，两位天文学家试图将画中的星星与 6 月中旬圣雷米的真实天空进行匹配。有人提出，天空是从 1889 年 6 月 19 日开始的，漩涡状星星的集合就是白羊座。

paras.en: But the other concluded it couldn’t have been painted on June 19, based on cloudy weather reports in Aix-en-Provence, France, about 70 kilometers away. That study claimed the painting was “a celestial composite, constructed to make an image of the morning sky.”
paras.zh: 但另一人根据约 70 公里外的法国普罗旺斯艾克斯的多云天气报告得出结论，这幅画不可能是在 6 月 19 日绘制的。该研究声称这幅画是“一幅天体合成作品，旨在描绘早晨的天空”。

paras.en: Kim, who founded a telescope-building company called SLLAB Inc. in Seoul, South Korea, didn’t know about the June date when he became interested in “The Starry Night.” “Unlike previous astronomical studies, we could start freely,” he says.
paras.zh: 金在韩国首尔创立了一家名为 SLLAB Inc. 的望远镜制造公司，他并不知道自己是在 6 月份对《星夜》产生兴趣的。 “与以前的天文学研究不同，我们可以自由地开始，”他说。

paras.en: Given his job, Kim had an intuition for which stars would be visible when. “People like me, who guide a telescope through its first alignment with the sky, naturally memorize where the stars are,” he says.
paras.zh: 鉴于他的工作，金有一种直觉，知道什么时候星星会出现。 “像我这样的人，第一次引导望远镜与天空对齐时，自然会记住星星的位置，”他说。

paras.en: He was skeptical of the Aries theory. The stars in that constellation are faint enough that they wouldn’t be all that visible in the predawn sky, “hardly enough to inspire a painter,” he says.
paras.zh: 他对白羊座理论持怀疑态度。这个星座中的星星非常暗淡，在黎明前的天空中不会那么明显，“几乎不足以激发画家的灵感，”他说。

paras.en: Instead, Kim saw the stars as the Hyades star cluster, which forms a sideways V shape in the constellation Taurus. To test that theory, he and his colleagues applied a statistical technique called Procrustes shape analysis to put a number to how well the stars in the painting matched any particular constellation.
paras.zh: 相反，金将这些恒星视为毕宿星团，它在金牛座中形成一个侧面的 V 形。为了检验这一理论，他和他的同事应用了一种称为普罗克拉斯特形状分析的统计技术，用一个数字来表示画中的星星与任何特定星座的匹配程度。

paras.en: Researchers compared the V-shaped collection of stars in “The Starry Night” (first image) with those in the Hyades star cluster (middle image). The resulting graph (last image) maps the real stars (blue) and the painting’s stars (orange) against each other. They don’t overlap perfectly, but they’re suspiciously close, researchers say. The label Sn stands for “The Starry Night.” while the constellation’s Greek letters represent typical astronomy notation.
paras.zh: 研究人员将“星夜”（第一张图片）中的 V 形恒星集合与毕宿星团（中图）中的恒星进行了比较。生成的图表（最后一张图片）将真实的星星（蓝色）和绘画中的星星（橙色）相互映射。研究人员表示，它们并不完全重叠，但非常接近。标签 Sn 代表“星夜”。而星座的希腊字母代表了典型的天文学符号。

paras.en: The team tested the method on another van Gogh skyscape, “Starry Night Over the Rhône,” which clearly depicts the Big Dipper. “Apart from the Big Dipper, there is no star pattern we can say for certain that Vincent painted,” Kim says. The degree of matching between the art and the sky for both paintings turned out to be similar, a major clue.
paras.zh: 该团队在梵高的另一幅天空景观《罗纳河上的星夜》中测试了该方法，该景观清楚地描绘了北斗七星。 “除了北斗七星之外，我们没有可以肯定地说文森特画过任何星星图案，”金说。两幅画的艺术与天空的匹配程度是相似的，这是一个重要线索。

paras.en: Kim also used the position and phase of the moon (a waxing gibbous on June 19, in contrast to the sharp waning crescent in the painting) and Venus to further constrain the painting’s date. He used computer simulations that weren’t available in the ‘80s to calculate the positions of celestial objects on certain dates in 1889 down to the second. He even traveled to France in June and July 2019 to try to find the field of view van Gogh would have seen from his window. Ultimately, July 22, 1889, was the best fit for the team’s data.
paras.zh: 金还利用月亮的位置和相位（6 月 19 日是盈凸月，与画中尖锐的渐亏新月形成鲜明对比）和金星来进一步限制这幅画的日期。他使用 80 年代无法使用的计算机模拟来计算 1889 年某些日期天体的位置，精确到秒。他甚至于 2019 年 6 月和 7 月前往法国，试图找到梵高从窗户看到的视野。最终，1889 年 7 月 22 日最适合该团队的数据。

paras.en: “I still cannot forget the moment we finally found the spot, overlaid the drawing on the view and saw it fit perfectly,” Kim says. “I was standing where Vincent had stood 130 years earlier. And the thrill I felt when I confirmed that the moon, the Hyades and Venus of July 22, 1889, fit exactly within the drawing’s field of view is still with me.”
paras.zh: “我仍然无法忘记我们最终找到地点，将图画覆盖在视图上并看到它完美契合的那一刻，”金说。 “我当时正站在文森特 130 年前站过的地方。当我确认 1889 年 7 月 22 日的月亮、毕星团和金星完全符合这幅画的视野时，我所感受到的激动仍然伴随着我。”

paras.en: Not to douse Kim’s enthusiasm, but that field of view may not be exactly what van Gogh saw, Olson says.
paras.zh: 奥尔森说，并不是要浇灭金的热情，但这种视野可能并不完全是梵高所看到的。

paras.en: “The authors’ assumed narrow field of view, essential for their theory that the stars of the Hyades fill most of the canvas, is inconsistent with the much wider field of view required to encompass ‘The Starry Night’s’ round hills and cliffs,” he says. That casts doubt on the paper’s conclusions.
paras.zh: “作者假设的狭窄视野，对于他们的理论来说至关重要，即毕星团的星星占据了画布的大部分，这与涵盖‘星夜’的圆形山丘和悬崖所需的更广阔的视野不一致，”他说。这让人对论文的结论产生怀疑。

paras.en: Olson proposes an experiment: Tell an amateur astronomer that “The Starry Night” depicts the Hyades and ask them to point out the star Aldebaran, which is at the bottom left of the V. In real life, this is the brightest star in the Hyades. But the painting has other much more prominent stars.
paras.zh: 奥尔森提出了一个实验：告诉一位业余天文学家，《星夜》描绘了毕星团，并要求他们指出位于V左下角的毕宿五星。在现实生活中，这是毕星团中最亮的恒星。但这幅画还有其他更突出的明星。

paras.en: “If [the authors’] theory is correct, then this should be easy,” Olson says. Kim and colleagues identify Aldebaran as one of the two stars to the left of the cypress tree in “The Starry Night.” But Olson thinks others will see it differently. “A decent guess is that an experienced amateur astronomer, even when prompted to see the Hyades, will not identify Aldebaran as either of the two stars to the left of the cypress tree.”
paras.zh: “如果[作者]的理论是正确的，那么这应该很容易，”奥尔森说。金和同事认为毕宿五是《星夜》中柏树左边的两颗星星之一。但奥尔森认为其他人会有不同的看法。 “一个合理的猜测是，一位经验丰富的业余天文学家，即使被提示去看毕星团，也不会认为毕宿五是柏树左边的两颗恒星中的任何一颗。”

articles.title: A nanoparticle revealed the tiny impact of a single gas atom
articles.author: Emily Conover

paras.en: It’s one of gentlest caresses imaginable: the touch of a single atom of gas. Now, scientists have measured its impact.
paras.zh: 这是可以想象到的最温柔的爱抚之一：单个气体原子的触摸。现在，科学家们已经测量了它的影响。

paras.en: A levitating nanoparticle jiggled when hit by individual gas atoms or molecules in a nearly empty vacuum chamber, scientists report in the October 23 Physical Review Letters.
paras.zh: 科学家在 10 月 23 日的《物理评论快报》上报告称，悬浮的纳米粒子在几乎空的真空室中受到单个气体原子或分子的撞击时会发生抖动。

paras.en: The force exerted by a gas is usually the result of many atoms or molecules bouncing around all at once: Think of the air inside a balloon keeping it inflated. But even an individual atom can exert a tiny force. To detect that force, researchers used a laser to levitate a glass sphere, just 100 nanometers across and weighing about a quadrillionth of a gram, inside a vacuum chamber. Then, the researchers added small amounts of a heavy gas, either krypton, xenon or sulfur hexafluoride. The first two are gases made up of atoms, while the third consists of molecules.
paras.zh: 气体施加的力通常是许多原子或分子同时弹跳的结果：想象一下气球内的空气使其保持膨胀。但即使是单个原子也能施加微小的力。为了检测这种力，研究人员使用激光使真空室内的一个玻璃球悬浮起来，该玻璃球直径仅为 100 纳米，重量约为万亿分之一克。然后，研究人员添加了少量的重气体，氪、氙或六氟化硫。前两种是由原子组成的气体，而第三种是由分子组成。

paras.en: The nanosphere was about 10 million times as massive as an individual gas particle, making the impact extremely difficult to detect. But, by monitoring the laser light that reflected from the sphere, the researchers could measure its tiny movements when hit by a gas particle. The resulting impulses were as small as a billionth of a Newton acting for one ten-trillionth of a second. And the rate of the collisions grew as the researchers introduced more gas into the chamber, increasing the pressure within.
paras.zh: 纳米球的质量约为单个气体粒子的 1000 万倍，因此影响极难检测。但是，通过监测从球体反射的激光，研究人员可以测量其被气体粒子撞击时的微小运动。由此产生的脉冲小至十亿分之一牛顿作用十万亿分之一秒。随着研究人员向室内引入更多气体，增加室内压力，碰撞率也随之增加。

paras.en: That suggests a possible application for the technique. “This could enable a very good way to sense pressure,” says physicist Yu-Han Tseng of Yale University, especially at very low pressures — such as in space or in vacuum chambers. The system could also distinguish between the different types of gases Tseng and colleagues studied, as each one interacted differently with the nanoparticle.
paras.zh: 这表明了该技术的可能应用。耶鲁大学物理学家 Yu-Han Tseng 表示：“这可以提供一种非常好的感知压力的方法，”特别是在非常低的压力下，例如在太空或真空室中。该系统还可以区分曾和同事研究的不同类型的气体，因为每种气体与纳米颗粒的相互作用都不同。

paras.en: A device like this could help reveal the composition of particles in space, and even on other worlds, Tseng says. “You can imagine putting it on another planet and [using] that to study the environment there.”
paras.zh: 曾说，这样的设备可以帮助揭示太空甚至其他世界的粒子成分。 “你可以想象把它放在另一个星球上并[用]它来研究那里的环境。”

articles.title: Herpes Virus Appears to Hijack The Brain's Immune Cells, And It Could Have Serious Consequences
articles.author: Peter Dockrill

paras.en: For many, the herpes virus is a pervasive pest that causes painful and unsightly blisters.
paras.zh: 对于许多人来说，疱疹病毒是一种普遍存在的害虫，会引起疼痛且难看的水泡。

paras.en: But the truth is far more concerning than any crusty cold sore.
paras.zh: 但事实远比任何硬皮唇疱疹更令人担忧。

paras.en: Research shows the herpes simplex virus (HSV-1) can infect the brain and nervous system, where it's been implicated in triggering Alzheimer's disease, possibly even doubling your risk of dementia.
paras.zh: 研究表明，单纯疱疹病毒 (HSV-1) 可以感染大脑和神经系统，从而引发阿尔茨海默病，甚至可能使患痴呆症的风险增加一倍。

paras.en: For a virus that plagues billions, it's vital we learn more about how HSV-1 infection works, and scientists just figured out a new piece of the puzzle.
paras.zh: 对于一种困扰数十亿人的病毒，我们必须更多地了解HSV-1感染的工作原理，科学家们刚刚找到了一个新的谜题。

paras.en: In a study in PLOS Pathogens, researchers found HSV-1 can basically reprogram immune cells called microglia in the brain, and the effects might help explain how the virus contributes to the inflammation seen in diseases of cognitive decline.
paras.zh: 在 PLOS Pathogens 的一项研究中，研究人员发现 HSV-1 基本上可以重新编程大脑中称为小胶质细胞的免疫细胞，其作用可能有助于解释该病毒如何导致认知能力下降疾病中的炎症。

paras.en: Microglia are specialized immune cells that continually monitor and maintain the brain by detecting threats, clearing out dead cells and damaged tissue, and pruning neuronal connections – but in the presence of the herpes virus, their ability to carry out healthy brain maintenance appears to be jeopardized.
paras.zh: 小胶质细胞是一种专门的免疫细胞，通过检测威胁、清除死亡细胞和受损组织以及修剪神经元连接来持续监控和维护大脑，但在疱疹病毒存在的情况下，它们进行健康大脑维护的能力似乎受到了损害。

paras.en: "When HSV-1 enters the brain, these cells shift into emergency defense mode," says neuroscientist Christy Niemeyer from the University of Colorado Anschutz.
paras.zh: “当 HSV-1 进入大脑时，这些细胞就会转入紧急防御模式，”科罗拉多大学安舒茨分校的神经科学家克里斯蒂·尼迈耶 (Christy Niemeyer) 说。

paras.en: "While this helps fight the virus, it may also compromise their ability to perform the everyday functions, even after the virus is gone."
paras.zh: “虽然这有助于对抗病毒，但即使在病毒消失后，也可能会损害他们执行日常功能的能力。”

paras.en: In experiments, researchers infected mice with HSV-1, then examined their brains six days later, using genetic analysis and imaging techniques to investigate the animals' immune responses and to map where the virus was present.
paras.zh: 在实验中，研究人员用 HSV-1 感染小鼠，然后在六天后检查它们的大脑，使用基因分析和成像技术来研究动物的免疫反应并绘制病毒存在的位置。

paras.en: The results showed the virus was confined to discrete spots in the brainstem, rather than spreading throughout it, and microglial activation markers were higher in regions of the brain found to contain the virus.
paras.zh: 结果显示，病毒被限制在脑干中的离散点，而不是在整个脑干中扩散，并且在发现含有病毒的大脑区域中，小胶质细胞激活标记物较高。

paras.en: What's more, activated microglia showed dramatically increased interferon signaling, in which the immune cells release proteins as chemical warning signs to other nearby cells.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，激活的小胶质细胞显示出显着增加的干扰素信号传导，其中免疫细胞释放蛋白质作为向附近其他细胞发出的化学警告信号。

paras.en: Compared to animals given a mock treatment, the proportion of interferon-responsive microglia was over 30 times higher in mice infected with HSV-1, suggesting the warning system could have gone into overdrive.
paras.zh: 与接受模拟治疗的动物相比，感染 HSV-1 的小鼠中干扰素反应性小胶质细胞的比例高出 30 倍以上，这表明预警系统可能已经过度运转。

paras.en: But that's not all. Affected cells also showed reduced expression of genes linked to normal brain maintenance, monitoring, and communication, suggesting a "redistribution of microglial identities" that could potentially have detrimental consequences for brain health.
paras.zh: 但这还不是全部。受影响的细胞还表现出与正常大脑维护、监测和交流相关的基因表达减少，这表明“小胶质细胞身份的重新分配”可能会对大脑健康产生不利后果。

paras.en: "Collectively, the suppression of these factors could impair microglial phagocytosis, clearance of neurotoxic factors, and promote protein aggregation, contributing to increased risk of neurodegenerative disease following HSV-1 infection," the researchers explain in their paper.
paras.zh: 研究人员在论文中解释道：“总的来说，抑制这些因素可能会损害小胶质细胞的吞噬作用、神经毒性因子的清除，并促进蛋白质聚集，从而增加 HSV-1 感染后患神经退行性疾病的风险。”

paras.en: "What makes these findings particularly interesting is that the virus isn't simply triggering inflammation," Niemeyer says.
paras.zh: 尼迈耶说：“这些发现特别有趣的是，这种病毒不仅仅会引发炎症。”

paras.en: "It's changing the molecular programs that control how these immune cells function. An important question is whether these changes persist after infection."
paras.zh: “它正在改变控制这些免疫细胞功能的分子程序。一个重要的问题是这些变化在感染后是否持续存在。”

paras.en: For now, we don't have the answer to that.
paras.zh: 目前，我们还没有答案。

paras.en: What we do have is evidence – if only in an animal model – that HSV-1 appears to override normal microglial function in a way that both promotes inflammation as a first-line response to the virus, while disrupting the immune cells' abilities to take care of the brain.
paras.zh: 我们所掌握的证据——如果仅在动物模型中——表明HSV-1似乎会超越正常的小胶质细胞功能，从而促进炎症作为对病毒的一线反应，同时破坏免疫细胞照顾大脑的能力。

paras.en: "Downregulation of these pathways suggests that HSV-1 infection shifts microglia away from their homeostatic maintenance functions toward a highly specialized antiviral state," the researchers explain.
paras.zh: 研究人员解释说：“这些途径的下调表明 HSV-1 感染使小胶质细胞从其稳态维持功能转向高度专业化的抗病毒状态。”

paras.en: "Loss of these homeostatic programs has been reported in multiple neurological disorders, including Alzheimer's disease and multiple sclerosis, raising the possibility that viral infection may initiate microglial state transitions that resemble those observed in neurodegenerative conditions."
paras.zh: “据报道，在多种神经系统疾病中，包括阿尔茨海默病和多发性硬化症，这些稳态程序的丧失，增加了病毒感染可能引发类似于神经退行性疾病中观察到的小胶质细胞状态转变的可能性。”

paras.en: It's worth emphasizing again that so far, we've only seen this immune response demonstrated in a small number of mice, and the animals were euthanized as part of the experiment, so we don't have proof that they would have gone on to develop neurodegeneration.
paras.zh: 值得再次强调的是，到目前为止，我们只在少数小鼠中看到了这种免疫反应，并且作为实验的一部分，这些动物被安乐死，所以我们没有证据表明它们会继续发展为神经退行性疾病。

paras.en: But if the same immune responses are taking place in humans infected with HSV-1, it's possible we've identified a critical pathway that contributes to cognitive decline.
paras.zh: 但如果感染 HSV-1 的人类也发生同样的免疫反应，我们就有可能发现了导致认知能力下降的关键途径。

paras.en: "Given the growing evidence linking HSV-1 to long-term neuroinflammatory phenotypes and Alzheimer's disease pathology, it is critical to explore the durability of these microglial state transitions," the researchers conclude.
paras.zh: 研究人员总结道：“鉴于越来越多的证据将 HSV-1 与长期神经炎症表型和阿尔茨海默病病理学联系起来，探索这些小胶质细胞状态转变的持久性至关重要。”

paras.en: "Our findings provide a mechanism linking acute viral infection to the long-term neuroinflammation that may precede neurological disease."
paras.zh: “我们的研究结果提供了一种将急性病毒感染与可能发生在神经系统疾病之前的长期神经炎症联系起来的机制。”

paras.en: The findings are reported in PLOS Pathogens.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在 PLOS Pathogens 杂志上。

articles.title: A Common Supplement Displays a Concerning Link to Heart Failure
articles.author: Carly Cassella

paras.en: One of the most popular supplements sold in the US could be having an unintended side effect, research suggests.
paras.zh: 研究表明，在美国销售的最受欢迎的补充剂之一可能会产生意想不到的副作用。

paras.en: Often promoted as a safe sleep aid, melatonin is a hormone-based supplement that many people can buy over the counter and take without much thought.
paras.zh: 褪黑激素经常被宣传为一种安全的睡眠辅助剂，它是一种基于激素的补充剂，许多人可以在柜台上购买并不假思索地服用。

paras.en: But preliminary research has some scientists worried about what happens when taking the supplement becomes a long-term habit.
paras.zh: 但初步研究让一些科学家担心，当服用补充剂成为长期习惯时会发生什么。

paras.en: A 2025 analysis of adults with insomnia has linked being prescribed melatonin for more than a year to a greater risk of heart issues.
paras.zh: 2025 年对患有失眠症的成年人进行的一项分析发现，服用褪黑激素超过一年会增加患心脏病的风险。

paras.en: Among more than 130,000 adults across multiple countries, those who were prescribed melatonin long-term were more at risk of heart failure and death in the following five years than those who were not prescribed it.
paras.zh: 在多个国家超过 130,000 名成年人中，长期服用褪黑激素的人在接下来的五年内比未服用褪黑激素的人更容易出现心力衰竭和死亡的风险。

paras.en: It found that people prescribed melatonin for more than a year had an 89 percent higher risk of heart failure over five years, and were about twice as likely to die from any cause.
paras.zh: 研究发现，服用褪黑激素超过一年的人在五年内患心力衰竭的风险增加了 89%，并且因任何原因死亡的可能性约为两倍。

paras.en: Watch the clip below for a summary of the findings:
paras.zh: 观看下面的剪辑以了解调查结果摘要：

paras.en: The research, which has not yet been peer-reviewed, was presented in November 2025 at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions.
paras.zh: 该研究尚未经过同行评审，已于 2025 年 11 月在美国心脏协会的科学会议上发表。

paras.en: The findings are preliminary. They do not prove that melatonin – the fourth most popular natural product taken by adults in the US – is causing dangerous repercussions.
paras.zh: 研究结果是初步的。他们并没有证明褪黑激素（美国成年人服用的第四大天然产品）正在造成危险的影响。

paras.en: But they do suggest that longer-term use needs closer study.
paras.zh: 但他们确实表明长期使用需要更仔细的研究。

paras.en: In April 2026, Saudi Arabia's drug regulator issued a formal safety signal on melatonin and heart failure, after reviewing global case reports alongside the study's findings, concluding the evidence so far is "suggestive for causal association". It's not a ban or a new warning label – but it's a sign regulators are starting to take the possibility seriously.
paras.zh: 2026 年 4 月，沙特阿拉伯药品监管机构在审查了全球病例报告以及研究结果后，发布了关于褪黑激素和心力衰竭的正式安全信号，得出的结论是，迄今为止的证据“暗示存在因果关系”。这不是禁令或新的警告标签，但这表明监管机构开始认真对待这种可能性。

paras.en: However, melatonin is typically considered safe and well-tolerated for short-term use among those who are not pregnant or breastfeeding. That means around 1 to 2 months.
paras.zh: 然而，对于未怀孕或未哺乳的人来说，褪黑激素通常被认为是安全且耐受性良好的短期使用。这意味着大约 1 到 2 个月。

paras.en: There are limited studies on the effects after that time, a situation that some researchers believe should be remedied, especially as the supplement grows in popularity.
paras.zh: 关于此后影响的研究有限，一些研究人员认为这种情况应该得到纠正，特别是随着补充剂越来越受欢迎。

paras.en: "Melatonin supplements may not be as harmless as commonly assumed," medical scientist Ekenedilichukwu Nnadi at SUNY Downstate/Kings County Primary Care in New York said.
paras.zh: 纽约州立大学下州/国王县初级保健中心的医学科学家 Ekenedilichukwu Nnadi 表示：“褪黑激素补充剂可能并不像人们普遍认为的那样无害。”

paras.en: A melatonin supplement replicates a hormone naturally produced by the brain to help keep the body's internal clock ticking. Taking this substitute at the end of the day can help some people fall asleep and stay asleep.
paras.zh: 褪黑激素补充剂复制大脑自然产生的激素，帮助保持身体的内部时钟滴答作响。在一天结束时服用这种替代品可以帮助一些人入睡并保持睡眠状态。

paras.en: In the US and many other nations, melatonin supplements are available over the counter, meaning patients can take them without medical guidance or supervision regarding dosage or duration of use.
paras.zh: 在美国和许多其他国家，褪黑激素补充剂可以在柜台购买，这意味着患者可以在没有医疗指导或剂量或使用时间监督的情况下服用它们。

paras.en: While some studies suggest that long-term melatonin use is safe, comprehensive research is lacking.
paras.zh: 虽然一些研究表明长期使用褪黑激素是安全的，但缺乏全面的研究。

paras.en: In the recent analysis, Nnadi and colleagues examined electronic health records from adults in the US and multiple other countries, including the UK, where melatonin is available only by prescription.
paras.zh: 在最近的分析中，纳迪和同事检查了美国和其他多个国家（包括英国）成年人的电子健康记录，在英国，褪黑激素只能通过处方获得。

paras.en: A secondary analysis found that those who took melatonin for over a year were almost 3.5 times as likely to be hospitalized for heart failure when compared to those not taking melatonin.
paras.zh: 二次分析发现，服用褪黑激素超过一年的人因心力衰竭住院的可能性是不服用褪黑激素的人的 3.5 倍。

paras.en: Plus, the risk of dying from any cause jumped from 4.3 percent to 7.8 percent between groups.
paras.zh: 此外，各组之间因任何原因死亡的风险从 4.3% 跃升至 7.8%。

paras.en: "Melatonin supplements are widely thought of as a safe and 'natural' option to support better sleep," said Nnadi.
paras.zh: “褪黑激素补充剂被广泛认为是支持更好睡眠的安全和‘天然’选择，”纳迪说。

paras.en: "So it was striking to see such consistent and significant increases in serious health outcomes, even after balancing for many other risk factors."
paras.zh: “因此，即使在平衡了许多其他风险因素之后，严重健康结果的持续和显着增加仍然令人震惊。”

paras.en: The findings are concerning, but they should be interpreted with caution. The study's methodology has a major limitation.
paras.zh: 研究结果令人担忧，但应谨慎解释。该研究的方法有一个重大局限性。

paras.en: Participants were not surveyed on their melatonin use.
paras.zh: 参与者没有接受有关褪黑激素使用情况的调查。

paras.en: Instead, prescription records were used to estimate who was taking the supplement.
paras.zh: 相反，处方记录被用来估计谁正在服用补充剂。

paras.en: That means the control group, made up of those who were not prescribed melatonin, may have included people in the US who bought melatonin over the counter and took it without a prescription.
paras.zh: 这意味着对照组（由未服用褪黑激素处方的人组成）可能包括在美国通过柜台购买褪黑激素并在没有处方的情况下服用的人。

paras.en: Carlos Egea, President of the Spanish Federation of Sleep Medicine Societies, who was not involved in the study, noted this caveat in an expert reaction to the research.
paras.zh: 西班牙睡眠医学会联合会主席卡洛斯·埃贾（Carlos Egea）没有参与这项研究，他在专家对这项研究的反应中指出了这一警告。

paras.en: However, he said the associations should be taken seriously.
paras.zh: 不过，他表示应该认真对待这些协会。

paras.en: "These findings challenge the perception of melatonin as a benign chronic therapy and only highlight the need for a prospective trial with a control group to clarify its safety profile," argued Egea.
paras.zh: Egea 认为：“这些发现挑战了褪黑激素作为良性慢性疗法的看法，并且仅强调需要进行对照组的前瞻性试验来阐明其安全性。”

paras.en: Related: Study Ties 5 Subtypes of Sleep With Distinct Health And Lifestyle Patterns
paras.zh: 相关：研究将 5 种睡眠亚型与不同的健康和生活方式模式联系起来

paras.en: Even in the short term, melatonin can come with downsides that many users may not know about.
paras.zh: 即使在短期内，褪黑激素也可能带来许多用户可能不知道的缺点。

paras.en: For instance, a series of non-fatal overdoses among children in Australia has raised questions about the safety profile of the supplement for certain age groups.
paras.zh: 例如，澳大利亚儿童发生的一系列非致命过量用药事件引发了人们对某些年龄段补充剂的安全性的质疑。

paras.en: Melatonin products may be based on a natural hormone, but that does not mean they are risk-free.
paras.zh: 褪黑激素产品可能基于天然激素，但这并不意味着它们没有风险。

paras.en: "If our study is confirmed, this could affect how doctors counsel patients about sleep aids," said Nnadi.
paras.zh: 纳迪说：“如果我们的研究得到证实，这可能会影响医生如何为患者提供有关睡眠辅助的咨询。”

paras.en: The findings were presented at the American Heart Association's Scientific Sessions in 2025.
paras.zh: 研究结果已在 2025 年美国心脏协会科学会议上公布。

articles.title: Mysterious Star Pattern in Famous Van Gogh Painting Solves a Century-Old Debate
articles.author: Esra Öz

paras.en: In 1889, Vincent van Gogh watched the sky before sunrise from his room at an asylum in Saint-Rémy, southern France.
paras.zh: 1889 年，文森特·梵高 (Vincent van Gogh) 在法国南部圣雷米一家精神病院的房间里观看日出前的天空。

paras.en: In a letter to his brother Theo, he recalled seeing only the morning star above the countryside before dawn, noting how large it appeared.
paras.zh: 在给弟弟西奥的一封信中，他回忆起黎明前只看到乡村上空的晨星，并注意到它有多大。

paras.en: In The Starry Night, painted that year, blue swirls sweep above a small village. A tall cypress rises on the left, while rings of yellow light surround the stars and crescent Moon.
paras.zh: 在当年创作的《星夜》中，蓝色漩涡席卷了一个小村庄的上空。左边矗立着一棵高大的柏树，黄色的光环围绕着星星和新月。

paras.en: According to New York's Museum of Modern Art, the painting drew inspiration from his window view. The village came from other views, however, and the cypress was brought closer. The museum identifies the bright light left of center as Venus, the morning star.
paras.zh: 据纽约现代艺术博物馆称，这幅画的灵感来自于他的窗外景色。然而，村庄来自不同的视角，柏树被拉近了。博物馆将中心左侧的明亮光线识别为金星，即晨星。

paras.en: Researchers in South Korea wanted to investigate how closely the arrangement of celestial objects reflected something Van Gogh had actually seen.
paras.zh: 韩国的研究人员想要调查天体的排列与梵高实际看到的事物的反映有多接近。

paras.en: Their study suggests that the Moon, Venus, and the central group of stars correspond to the sky visible before dawn around 22 July 1889. The match supports the possibility that Van Gogh incorporated an observed sky into his expressive composition.
paras.zh: 他们的研究表明，月亮、金星和中央恒星群对应于 1889 年 7 月 22 日左右黎明前可见的天空。这一匹配支持了梵高将观察到的天空融入到他的表现力构图中的可能性。

paras.en: Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim, a PhD candidate at Kyung Hee University's School of Space Research and CEO of South Korean telescope maker SLLAB, led the investigation.
paras.zh: 庆熙大学空间研究学院博士研究生、韩国望远镜制造商 SLLAB 首席执行官 Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim 领导了这项调查。

paras.en: A familiar pattern near the painting's center had caught his attention: a V-shaped star cluster called the Hyades, in the Bull constellation, Taurus. Earlier research had proposed stars in the Ram constellation, Aries, but the astronomical interpretations had remained unsettled.
paras.zh: 画作中心附近一个熟悉的图案引起了他的注意：一个名为毕星团的 V 形星团，位于金牛座的公牛座中。早期的研究提出了白羊座中的恒星，但天文解释仍然悬而未决。

paras.en: There was also a problem with the Moon. The painting is conventionally dated to June 1889, when the Moon around the middle of the month was more than half illuminated. "The strongest evidence is the sky itself," Kim told ScienceAlert. "The waning gibbous moon around 18 June does not match the slender crescent in the painting."
paras.zh: 月球也有一个问题。这幅画的创作时间传统上是 1889 年 6 月，当时月中左右的月亮被照亮了一半以上。 “最有力的证据是天空本身，”金告诉 ScienceAlert。 “6月18日左右的亏凸月与画中细长的新月并不相符。”

paras.en: To examine these clues together, the team returned to Van Gogh's landscapes.
paras.zh: 为了共同检验这些线索，研究小组回到了梵高的风景画。

paras.en: During two field trips to France in 2019, they photographed places he had drawn and painted. Comparing buildings, bridges, and landscape features with his pictures helped them estimate how narrowly he had framed the scenery.
paras.zh: 在 2019 年两次去法国实地考察期间，他们拍摄了他画过的地方。将建筑物、桥梁和景观特征与他的照片进行比较，有助于他们估计他对风景的构图有多狭隘。

paras.en: They tested their approach on two night scenes he painted in Arles in 1888. In Café Terrace at Night, they identified a possible match with three bright stars forming the Summer Triangle.
paras.zh: 他们在他 1888 年在阿尔勒画的两幅夜景中测试了他们的方法。在《夜晚的露台咖啡馆》中，他们发现了与形成夏季大三角的三颗明亮星星的可能匹配。

paras.en: For The Starry Night, they applied a viewing frame derived from an earlier drawing associated with its village landscape to computer reconstructions of the 1889 sky.
paras.zh: 在《星夜》中，他们将源自一幅早期与其村庄景观相关的绘画中衍生的观察框架应用到了 1889 年天空的计算机重建中。

paras.en: Among the June and July dawns when the Moon sat above Venus, as in the painting, June 23 and July 22–23 placed both within the reconstructed frame. Around July 22, the Hyades also occupied the center, producing the closest match to the painting.
paras.zh: 正如画中所示，在六月和七月的黎明期间，月亮位于金星上方，6 月 23 日和 7 月 22 日至 23 日都位于重建的框架内。 7月22日左右，毕宿星团也占据了中心，产生了与画作最接近的匹配。

paras.en: The researchers then measured the relative positions of five central stars on the canvas. A mathematical method that rotates, shifts, and uniformly resizes patterns found a close correspondence with the Hyades. For those five selected points, every alternative pairing with the Hyades stars produced a worse fit.
paras.zh: 然后研究人员测量了画布上五颗中心恒星的相对位置。一种旋转、移动和统一调整图案大小的数学方法与毕宿星团有着密切的对应关系。对于这五个选定的点，与毕宿星星的每一个替代配对都会产生更差的拟合。

paras.en: The match was closer in Van Gogh's later pen drawing of the painting. The star group's tilt relative to the horizon also agreed with the reconstructed sky.
paras.zh: 在梵高后来的钢笔画中，这种匹配更为接近。星群相对于地平线的倾斜也与重建的天空一致。

paras.en: The researchers suggest that the approach could help art historians reassess how the painting developed. They argue that Van Gogh may still have been working on the canvas in July, after beginning it in June, and that similar comparisons could help investigate the skies depicted in other historical night paintings.
paras.zh: 研究人员表示，这种方法可以帮助艺术史学家重新评估这幅画的发展过程。他们认为，梵高在六月开始创作这幅画后，可能仍在七月继续创作，类似的比较可以帮助研究其他历史夜间画作中描绘的天空。

paras.en: The July interpretation raises questions about the established chronology. Van Gogh mentioned a new starry-sky study in a June 18 letter, but the researchers argue that this does not show he had finished the painting.
paras.zh: 七月的解释对既定的年表提出了质疑。梵高在 6 月 18 日的一封信中提到了一项新的星空研究，但研究人员认为这并不表明他已经完成了这幅画。

paras.en: They also suggest that an episode of illness usually placed in mid-July began later, leaving open the possibility that he observed the sky around July 22. Letters and historical weather records support their interpretation, but no medical notes from the time show when the illness began.
paras.zh: 他们还认为，通常在 7 月中旬发生的一次疾病开始得较晚，因此他有可能在 7 月 22 日左右观察到了天空。信件和历史天气记录支持他们的解释，但没有任何医疗记录显示疾病何时开始。

paras.en: The astronomical comparison also needs several clues to work together. Other star groups produced close geometric matches, so shape alone cannot identify the painted stars.
paras.zh: 天文比较也需要几条线索共同作用。其他星星群产生了紧密的几何匹配，因此仅凭形状无法识别彩绘的星星。

paras.en: The Hyades interpretation gains support from the stars' relative positions, the arrangement of the Moon and Venus, and the way the Moon, Venus, and the Hyades fit together within the reconstructed frame.
paras.zh: 毕星团的解释得到了恒星的相对位置、月球和金星的排列，以及月球、金星和毕星团在重建框架内的组合方式的支持。

paras.en: "What our study shows is that the sky in the painting matches, in both observation and shape, the real pre-dawn sky around 22 July. That alone does not pin the completion of the painting down to a single day," Kim explained.
paras.zh: “我们的研究表明，画中的天空在观察和形状上都与 7 月 22 日左右黎明前的真实天空相匹配。仅凭这一点并不能将这幅画的完成时间确定为某一天，”Kim 解释道。

paras.en: "I believe Vincent brought together on a single canvas the skies of several days before and after 22 July."
paras.zh: “我相信文森特将 7 月 22 日前后几天的天空汇集在一张画布上。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Scientific Reports.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学报告》上。

articles.title: A revolutionary new microscope could reveal the hidden machinery of life

paras.en: A revolutionary new microscope could reveal the hidden machinery of life
paras.zh: 革命性的新型显微镜可以揭示隐藏的生命机制

paras.en: A revolutionary laser-powered microscope could reveal a hidden world inside human cells, opening an entirely new window into life and disease.
paras.zh: 革命性的激光显微镜可以揭示人体细胞内隐藏的世界，为了解生命和疾病打开一扇全新的窗口。

paras.en: - Researchers have developed a revolutionary microscope that uses an incredibly powerful laser to make previously invisible cellular structures easier to see. The technology dramatically improves image clarity, allowing scientists to examine small proteins that conventional electron microscopes struggle to capture. It could eventually reveal how tiny molecular machines interact inside cells, providing an unprecedented look at the hidden workings of life.
paras.zh: - 研究人员开发了一种革命性的显微镜，它使用极其强大的激光，使以前看不见的细胞结构变得更容易看到。该技术极大地提高了图像清晰度，使科学家能够检查传统电子显微镜难以捕获的小蛋白质。它最终可能揭示微小的分子机器如何在细胞内相互作用，为生命隐藏的运作提供前所未有的视角。

paras.en: Almost a century ago, a breakthrough in microscopy gave scientists an entirely new way to examine the inside of cells. Known as phase contrast, the technique made previously faint or nearly invisible cellular structures much easier to distinguish. Its importance was recognized with a Nobel Prize in 1953.
paras.zh: 大约一个世纪前，显微镜技术的突破为科学家提供了一种检查细胞内部的全新方法。这项技术被称为相差技术，使以前微弱或几乎看不见的细胞结构变得更容易区分。 1953 年，它的重要性得到了诺贝尔奖的认可。

paras.en: Now, physicists at the University of California, Berkeley, have brought that same principle to electron microscopy, a technology capable of magnifying objects roughly 10,000 times more than conventional light microscopes.
paras.zh: 现在，加州大学伯克利分校的物理学家将同样的原理引入了电子显微镜，这种技术能够将物体放大到传统光学显微镜大约 10,000 倍。

paras.en: The researchers have developed a device called a laser phase plate that could significantly improve cryoelectron microscopy (cryo-EM). This powerful imaging method has transformed the study of protein structures and helped speed up drug discovery over the past decade. Even so, it has a major limitation: Most human proteins are so small that obtaining clear images of them remains extremely difficult.
paras.zh: 研究人员开发了一种称为激光相位板的设备，可以显着改善冷冻电子显微镜（cryo-EM）。这种强大的成像方法改变了蛋白质结构的研究，并在过去十年中帮助加速了药物发现。即便如此，它也有一个重大限制：大多数人类蛋白质都很小，因此获得它们的清晰图像仍然极其困难。

paras.en: The new laser technology could help overcome that obstacle, potentially allowing scientists to image proteins as small as one-third the size of those that challenge current microscopes.
paras.zh: 新的激光技术可以帮助克服这一障碍，有可能使科学家能够对小至目前显微镜所无法比拟的蛋白质三分之一大小的蛋白质进行成像。

paras.en: An even greater impact could come from improvements to cryoelectron tomography (cryo-ET). This newer approach combines images captured from multiple angles to construct three-dimensional views of proteins and other molecules. Unlike techniques that study isolated molecules in a solution, cryo-ET can reveal how proteins are arranged and interact within their natural cellular surroundings.
paras.zh: 冷冻电子断层扫描 (cryo-ET) 的改进可能会产生更大的影响。这种新方法结合了从多个角度捕获的图像来构建蛋白质和其他分子的三维视图。与研究溶液中孤立分子的技术不同，冷冻电子断层扫描可以揭示蛋白质在其自然细胞环境中的排列和相互作用。

paras.en: “Cryo-EM has become the new, fastest-growing method for resolving the structure of biological macromolecules, and cryo-ET is expected to show how these molecules work together in their natural, cellular context,” said Holger Müller, a UC Berkeley professor of physics and faculty scientist at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory who led the development effort. “But because of signal-to-noise limitations, the majority of human and animal proteins are too small to be analyzed by these methods. The increase in signal-to-noise ratio provided by this laser phase plate is expected to overcome these important limitations.”
paras.zh: “冷冻电镜已经成为解析生物大分子结构的新的、增长最快的方法，冷冻电镜有望展示这些分子在自然细胞环境中如何协同工作，”领导这项开发工作的加州大学伯克利分校物理学教授、劳伦斯伯克利国家实验室的科学家 Holger Müller 说。 “但由于信噪比的限制，大多数人类和动物蛋白质都太小，无法通过这些方法进行分析。这种激光相位板提供的信噪比的增加有望克服这些重要的限制。”

paras.en: An Extraordinary Laser Reveals Hidden Cellular Structures
paras.zh: 非凡的激光揭示隐藏的细胞结构

paras.en: The breakthrough relies on what the researchers describe as the world's most intense focused continuous-wave laser. Rather than simply illuminating a specimen, the laser interacts directly with the microscope's electron beam, altering its phase to increase image contrast.
paras.zh: 这一突破依赖于研究人员所描述的世界上最强的聚焦连续波激光器。激光不是简单地照亮样本，而是直接与显微镜的电子束相互作用，改变其相位以增加图像对比度。

paras.en: This adjustment makes it easier to distinguish small molecules, including hemoglobin, from their surroundings. It could also improve the visibility of structures inside cells, such as the nucleus and mitochondria.
paras.zh: 这种调整使得更容易将包括血红蛋白在内的小分子与其周围环境区分开来。它还可以提高细胞内部结构的可见性，例如细胞核和线粒体。

paras.en: “With cryo-ET, we're looking at small, very complicated cellular material that’s incredibly crowded inside the cell,” said Bridget Carragher, founding technical director of imaging at Biohub in Redwood City, California. “It’s like a forest of trees, and you’re trying to find one leaf on one tree in there. Cryo-ET needs a dramatic step forward in contrast, so we can start to see what's going on inside the cell. That's what the laser phase plate promises to give us.”
paras.zh: “通过冷冻电子断层扫描，我们正在研究微小、非常复杂的细胞材料，这些材料在细胞内极其拥挤，”加利福尼亚州雷德伍德城 Biohub 成像技术总监 Bridget Carragher 说。 “这就像一片树林，你试图在其中的一棵树上找到一片叶子。冷冻电子断层扫描需要在对比方面向前迈出一大步，这样我们才能开始看到细胞内部发生了什么。这就是激光相位板承诺给我们的。”

paras.en: With financial support from Biohub, Müller acquired an advanced cryo-EM instrument and equipped it with the new laser phase plate. He named the resulting microscope Theia, after the ancient Greek Titaness associated with light and radiance.
paras.zh: 在 Biohub 的资金支持下，Müller 购买了先进的冷冻电镜仪器，并为其配备了新型激光相位板。他将由此产生的显微镜命名为忒伊亚（Theia），以古希腊与光和光芒相关的泰坦女神的名字命名。

paras.en: Meanwhile, Carragher is directing the construction of a related microscope at Biohub's imaging facility in Redwood City. Her team's instrument uses two lasers rather than one, building on theoretical research conducted by Müller and his collaborators.
paras.zh: 与此同时，卡拉格正在雷德伍德城的 Biohub 成像设施中指导建造相关的显微镜。她的团队的仪器基于 Müller 及其合作者进行的理论研究，使用两个而不是一个激光器。

paras.en: The two laser beams are arranged at right angles to one another and each operates at approximately half the power. This configuration helps prevent components from burning out while also reducing optical distortions that could interfere with image quality.
paras.zh: 两束激光束彼此成直角排列，每束激光束的工作功率约为一半。这种配置有助于防止组件烧坏，同时还减少可能影响图像质量的光学失真。

paras.en: Both research teams are working with Thermo Fisher Scientific, the leading manufacturer of cryo-EM instruments.
paras.zh: 两个研究团队均与冷冻电镜仪器的领先制造商 Thermo Fisher Scientific 合作。

paras.en: “Theia is the Formula 1 microscope,” Müller said. “It has extra electron optics that give it better resolution than the standard cryo-EM, even without the laser. With the addition of the laser phase plate, we hope that it really becomes the world's best instrument overall.”
paras.zh: “Theia 是一级方程式显微镜，”穆勒说。 “它具有额外的电子光学器件，即使没有激光，也能提供比标准冷冻电镜更好的分辨率。通过添加激光相位板，我们希望它真正成为世界上最好的仪器。”

paras.en: The Berkeley team's latest images and technical findings are presented in the journal Science. Details of Biohub's two-laser design are available in a recently posted preprint.
paras.zh: 伯克利团队的最新图像和技术发现发表在《科学》杂志上。 Biohub 的两激光器设计的详细信息可在最近发布的预印本中找到。

paras.en: How a Nobel Prize-Winning Discovery Changed Microscopy
paras.zh: 诺贝尔奖获奖发现如何改变显微镜技术

paras.en: To understand why the new technology matters, it helps to look at a longstanding challenge in biological imaging.
paras.zh: 要了解新技术的重要性，有助于了解生物成像领域长期存在的挑战。

paras.en: Because plant and animal cells consist largely of water, they are relatively transparent when viewed under an ordinary light microscope. Although this transparency might seem beneficial, it creates a problem. Small cellular structures, including mitochondria and nuclei, scatter very little light and therefore appear only slightly darker than the surrounding material.
paras.zh: 由于植物和动物细胞主要由水组成，因此在普通光学显微镜下观察时，它们相对透明。尽管这种透明度似乎有益，但它却产生了问题。小细胞结构，包括线粒体和细胞核，散射的光非常少，因此看起来只比周围材料稍暗。

paras.en: Scientists have traditionally addressed this problem by adding stains to create greater contrast. However, staining also kills the cells.
paras.zh: 科学家传统上通过添加染色剂来产生更大的对比度来解决这个问题。然而，染色也会杀死细胞。

paras.en: In 1930, Dutch physicist Frits Zernike realized that light passing through biological material changes in more ways than simply becoming brighter or dimmer. When light scatters inside a cell, it also experiences a tiny delay that changes its phase, or the timing of its wave peaks.
paras.zh: 1930 年，荷兰物理学家 Frits Zernike 意识到，穿过生物材料的光会以多种方式发生变化，而不仅仅是变得更亮或更暗。当光在细胞内散射时，它也会经历微小的延迟，从而改变其相位或波峰的时间。

paras.en: Although the human eye cannot directly detect this phase shift, Zernike discovered that it could be converted into a visible difference in brightness. By shifting the phase of the unscattered light by 90 degrees, he made subtle cellular features stand out more clearly against their background when the light reached the viewer's eye.
paras.zh: 尽管人眼无法直接检测到这种相移，但泽尼克发现它可以转化为可见的亮度差异。通过将未散射光的相位移动 90 度，当光到达观察者的眼睛时，他使微妙的细胞特征在背景下更加清晰地突出。

paras.en: This innovation became the foundation of phase-contrast microscopy, earning Zernike the 1953 Nobel Prize in Physics.
paras.zh: 这项创新成为相差显微镜的基础，泽尼克因此获得 1953 年诺贝尔物理学奖。

paras.en: By the early 1940s, scientists had already recognized how useful phase contrast was for studying cells. They began exploring whether the same idea might improve electron microscopes, which use electrons instead of light to examine structures as small as individual proteins.
paras.zh: 到 20 世纪 40 年代初，科学家们已经认识到相差对于研究细胞有多么有用。他们开始探索同样的想法是否可以改进电子显微镜，电子显微镜使用电子而不是光来检查小到单个蛋白质的结构。

paras.en: Unfortunately, early attempts encountered serious technical difficulties. Devices designed to alter the phase of electron beams often weakened the beam too much, introduced image instability, or reduced resolution.
paras.zh: 不幸的是，早期的尝试遇到了严重的技术困难。设计用于改变电子束相位的设备通常会过度削弱电子束，导致图像不稳定或分辨率降低。

paras.en: A possible solution emerged in 2010, when Müller and Robert Glaeser, now a UC Berkeley professor emeritus of molecular and cell biology, proposed using an intense laser to produce the necessary phase shift. Their approach offered a way to improve contrast without sacrificing electron beam intensity.
paras.zh: 2010 年，Müller 和加州大学伯克利分校分子与细胞生物学名誉教授 Robert Glaeser 提出了一种可能的解决方案，他们提议使用强激光来产生必要的相移。他们的方法提供了一种在不牺牲电子束强度的情况下提高对比度的方法。

paras.en: Overcoming the Limits of Electron Microscopy
paras.zh: 克服电子显微镜的局限性

paras.en: Glaeser has played an important role in developing cryo-EM, which offers a potentially simpler way to determine molecular structures than traditional X-ray crystallography.
paras.zh: Glaeser 在开发冷冻电镜方面发挥了重要作用，冷冻电镜提供了一种比传统 X 射线晶体学可能更简单的确定分子结构的方法。

paras.en: X-ray crystallography requires researchers to grow crystals of the molecules they want to study and obtain access to an intense X-ray source. Cryo-EM avoids the need to crystallize molecules, but it presents difficulties of its own.
paras.zh: X 射线晶体学要求研究人员生长他们想要研究的分子晶体，并获得强 X 射线源。冷冻电镜无需使分子结晶，但它本身也存在困难。

paras.en: One of the biggest problems is that an electron beam can heat and eventually damage the specimen being examined. This limits how much information can be collected and how detailed the resulting images can become. Covering specimens with metal can reduce damage and improve contrast, but it also makes the images less sharp.
paras.zh: 最大的问题之一是电子束会加热并最终损坏被检查的样本。这限制了可以收集的信息量以及生成的图像的详细程度。用金属覆盖样本可以减少损坏并提高对比度，但也会降低图像的清晰度。

paras.en: During the 1960s, researchers began investigating whether freezing biological samples could protect them from radiation damage.
paras.zh: 20 世纪 60 年代，研究人员开始研究冷冻生物样本是否可以保护它们免受辐射损伤。

paras.en: Glaeser demonstrated that cooling specimens helped preserve them during imaging. He also proposed using a less intense electron beam to examine thousands of frozen molecules at once, further limiting the damage.
paras.zh: 格莱泽证明，冷却标本有助于在成像过程中保存它们。他还建议使用强度较低的电子束一次检查数千个冷冻分子，进一步限制损害。

paras.en: Because the molecules would be positioned at different angles, computers could analyze and combine their images to reconstruct a highly detailed molecular structure.
paras.zh: 由于分子会以不同的角度定位，因此计算机可以分析并组合它们的图像，以重建高度详细的分子结构。

paras.en: These advances helped establish the foundations of modern cryo-EM, whose developers received the 2017 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. During their acceptance remarks, the Nobel laureates acknowledged Glaeser's contributions.
paras.zh: 这些进步帮助奠定了现代冷冻电镜的基础，其开发者获得了 2017 年诺贝尔化学奖。诺贝尔奖获得者在获奖感言中承认了格莱泽的贡献。

paras.en: The Nobel Committee praised the technology, explaining that cryo-EM “both simplifies and improves the imaging of biomolecules. This method has moved biochemistry into a new era.”
paras.zh: 诺贝尔委员会赞扬了这项技术，并解释说冷冻电镜“既简化又改善了生物分子的成像。这种方法将生物化学带入了一个新时代。”

paras.en: A 15-Year Quest to Harness an Exceptionally Powerful Laser
paras.zh: 15 年探索如何驾驭超强激光

paras.en: Turning the laser phase plate concept into working technology required years of engineering.
paras.zh: 将激光相位板概念转化为实用技术需要多年的工程设计。

paras.en: Following their 2010 proposal, Müller spent 15 years pursuing the idea, with part of the research supported by the National Institutes of Health.
paras.zh: 根据 2010 年的提案，Müller 花了 15 年的时间来追求这个想法，部分研究得到了美国国立卫生研究院的支持。

paras.en: The first major challenge was generating an extraordinarily intense laser beam concentrated into a tiny area. The researchers needed enough light intensity to change the phase of an electron beam by 90 degrees.
paras.zh: 第一个主要挑战是产生集中在一个微小区域的异常强烈的激光束。研究人员需要足够的光强度才能将电子束的相位改变 90 度。

paras.en: It took a decade to develop the necessary system.
paras.zh: 开发必要的系统花了十年时间。

paras.en: Their solution was to confine a continuous laser beam inside a spherical chamber lined with mirrors. As the light repeatedly reflected through the cavity more than 10,000 times, its intensity increased dramatically while the beam became focused into an extremely small spot.
paras.zh: 他们的解决方案是将连续激光束限制在衬有镜子的球形室内。当光通过腔体重复反射超过 10,000 次时，其强度急剧增加，同时光束聚焦成一个极小的光斑。

paras.en: “It’s 75 kilowatts focused to a few microns,” Müller said. “That’s more powerful than what you use for welding. It's more power than a military laser. It builds up the brightest continuous laser focus ever.”
paras.zh: “它的功率为 75 千瓦，聚焦于几微米，”穆勒说。 “这比焊接所用的功率更强大。它比军用激光器的功率更大。它建立了有史以来最亮的连续激光焦点。”

paras.en: The team first demonstrated that the concept worked by installing a laser phase plate in one of Glaeser's older electron microscopes.
paras.zh: 该团队首先通过在 Glaeser 的一台旧电子显微镜中安装激光相位板来证明这一概念的有效性。

paras.en: Additional funding from Biohub then made it possible to acquire a customized, state-of-the-art Thermo Fisher Krios cryo-EM microscope and modify it to accommodate the laser technology.
paras.zh: 随后，Biohub 提供额外资金，使我们能够购买定制的、最先进的 Thermo Fisher Krios 冷冻电镜显微镜，并对其进行修改以适应激光技术。

paras.en: In their latest research, the scientists tested the upgraded microscope using six different samples that varied in size and preparation method. The laser consistently improved image resolution, with particularly important gains for specimens that are difficult to image using standard methods.
paras.zh: 在最新的研究中，科学家们使用六种不同尺寸和制备方法的不同样品测试了升级后的显微镜。激光不断提高图像分辨率，对于难以使用标准方法成像的样本来说，效果尤其显着。

paras.en: “For the most challenging cases — small particles, bad specimens — the laser produces a very considerable advantage,” Müller said.
paras.zh: “对于最具挑战性的情况——小颗粒、不良样本——激光产生了非常大的优势，”穆勒说。

paras.en: Sharper Images of Proteins Once Too Small to Study
paras.zh: 曾经太小而无法研究的蛋白质的更清晰图像

paras.en: To demonstrate the new microscope's capabilities, the researchers reconstructed images of two different proteins.
paras.zh: 为了展示新显微镜的功能，研究人员重建了两种不同蛋白质的图像。

paras.en: The first was aldolase, a protein found in muscle that modern cryo-EM systems can already image relatively easily. The second was hemoglobin, the protein responsible for carrying oxygen through the bloodstream.
paras.zh: 第一个是醛缩酶，这是一种在肌肉中发现的蛋白质，现代冷冻电镜系统已经可以相对容易地对其进行成像。第二种是血红蛋白，这种蛋白质负责在血液中携带氧气。

paras.en: Hemoglobin is much smaller and lies near the lower size limit of proteins that conventional cryo-EM instruments can reliably analyze.
paras.zh: 血红蛋白要小得多，接近传统冷冻电镜仪器可以可靠分析的蛋白质尺寸下限。

paras.en: Using the laser phase plate, the researchers improved the resolution of both protein structures. The improvement was especially pronounced for hemoglobin, highlighting the technology's potential to overcome the difficulties associated with smaller molecules.
paras.zh: 使用激光相位板，研究人员提高了两种蛋白质结构的分辨率。对于血红蛋白来说，这种改进尤其明显，突显了该技术克服与较小分子相关的困难的潜力。

paras.en: “The bottom line is, if you have a large protein and a really good sample — a fresh one or one frozen without bubbles, for example — you may not need the phase plate to get a single, high-quality image. But for a small protein and a bad sample, laser-on is best,” Müller said. “This could fill an enormous gap in our knowledge of protein structures that can’t be crystallized or are too small for today’s cryo-EM. And it will be revolutionary for cryo-ET.”
paras.zh: “底线是，如果你有大量蛋白质和非常好的样品——例如新鲜的样品或没有气泡的冷冻样品——你可能不需要相位板来获得单一的高质量图像。但对于少量蛋白质和质量较差的样品，激光是最好的，”Müller 说。 “这可以填补我们对蛋白质结构的巨大空白，这些蛋白质结构对于当今的冷冻电子显微镜来说无法结晶或太小。这对于冷冻电子断层扫描来说将是革命性的。”

paras.en: Protein mass is typically expressed in daltons, a unit named after English chemist John Dalton. One dalton is defined as one-twelfth the mass of a carbon-12 atom.
paras.zh: 蛋白质质量通常以道尔顿表示，这是一个以英国化学家约翰·道尔顿命名的单位。一道尔顿定义为碳 12 原子质量的十二分之一。

paras.en: Conventional cryo-EM struggles to image proteins smaller than approximately 70 kilodaltons. That limitation is particularly significant because proteins below this threshold account for about 90% of the human proteome, the complete collection of proteins produced by the human body.
paras.zh: 传统的冷冻电镜很难对小于大约 70 道尔顿的蛋白质进行成像。这种限制尤其重要，因为低于该阈值的蛋白质约占人类蛋白质组（人体产生的蛋白质的完整集合）的 90%。

paras.en: With the laser phase plate, researchers can now image proteins as small as 50 kilodaltons, although doing so remains challenging. Such proteins are even smaller than hemoglobin.
paras.zh: 借助激光相位板，研究人员现在可以对小至 50 千道尔顿的蛋白质进行成像，尽管这样做仍然具有挑战性。这些蛋白质甚至比血红蛋白还要小。

paras.en: The Next Goal Is to Reveal Even Smaller Proteins
paras.zh: 下一个目标是揭示更小的蛋白质

paras.en: Müller believes the technology could eventually allow scientists to study proteins as small as 17 kilodaltons (the size of the protein myoglobin).
paras.zh: Müller 相信这项技术最终可以让科学家研究小至 17 千道尔顿（蛋白质肌红蛋白的大小）的蛋白质。

paras.en: Reaching that goal may require another improvement: using a tightly focused electron beam rather than the defocused beam currently needed to produce sufficient contrast without the laser phase plate.
paras.zh: 实现这一目标可能需要另一项改进：使用紧密聚焦的电子束，而不是目前需要的散焦光束，以在没有激光相位板的情况下产生足够的对比度。

paras.en: According to Müller, the laser system should make it possible to obtain contrast directly from phase changes in a focused electron beam.
paras.zh: 根据穆勒的说法，激光系统应该能够直接从聚焦电子束的相位变化中获得对比度。

paras.en: If successful, this adjustment could double the contrast and signal-to-noise ratio again, adding to the improvement already achieved with the laser phase plate.
paras.zh: 如果成功，这种调整可以使对比度和信噪比再次加倍，从而进一步提高激光相位板已经实现的改进。

paras.en: Such progress could make it possible to study a far larger proportion of the body's proteins and provide unprecedented insight into how they interact within the complex environment of cells.
paras.zh: 这些进展可以使研究更大比例的人体蛋白质成为可能，并为它们如何在复杂的细胞环境中相互作用提供前所未有的见解。

paras.en: “This technology is a step function change for biology,” said Stephani Otte, Biohub’s Vice President of Imaging Science. “We are going to be able to see how molecular machines operate inside the living cell, in context, for the first time. What was once invisible will become visible — and that changes everything about how we understand disease.”
paras.zh: Biohub 影像科学副总裁 Stephani Otte 表示：“这项技术是生物学的阶跃功能变革。” “我们将能够第一次看到分子机器如何在活细胞内运作。曾经不可见的东西将变得可见——这改变了我们理解疾病的方式。”

paras.en: The Berkeley research team also includes Glaeser; postdoctoral fellows and co-first authors Petar Petrov and Jessie Zhang; staff scientist Jonathan Remis; postdoctoral fellow Hang Cheng; and current and former physics graduate students Jeremy Axelrod, Eric Cooper, Ian Hicklin, Shahar Sandhaus, and Cooper Schnurr.
paras.zh: 伯克利研究团队还包括 Glaeser；博士后研究员和共同第一作者 Petar Petrov 和 Jessie 张；研究员乔纳森·雷米斯；博士后程航；以及现任和前任物理学研究生 Jeremy Axelrod、Eric Cooper、Ian Hicklin、Shahar Sandhaus 和 Cooper Schnurr。

paras.en: At Biohub, Carragher and David Agard, the organization's founding scientific director of imaging, jointly lead the Dynamic Structural Cell Biology group. Both are co-corresponding authors of the Biohub preprint, alongside Biohub engineer Pavel Olshin.
paras.zh: 在 Biohub，卡拉格和该组织创始成像科学总监 David Agard 共同领导动态结构细胞生物学小组。两人与 Biohub 工程师 Pavel Olshin 都是 Biohub 预印本的共同通讯作者。

paras.en: Materials provided by University of California - Berkeley. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由加州大学伯克利分校提供。注意：内容可能会根据样式和长度进行编辑。
